**Scenario:** the primary fails over for five seconds, or `helm upgrade` restarts the worker while people are working. Every event read in that window is never handled: no audit entry, no inbox item, no webhook delivery, no rule run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A consumer acknowledges only after success, or after a permanent error. After N attempts the event is moved to a dead-letter record an administrator can see.
- [ ] On start and periodically, each group claims its own pending entries (`XAUTOCLAIM` with a minimum idle time) and handles them.
- [ ] A shutdown finishes or abandons the batch with a context that is not cancelled, so nothing is half-handled.
- [ ] Handlers stay idempotent by event id, as the decision says.

## Tests

- **Integration (with the stack's Valkey):**
  - a handler that fails once is retried and succeeds;
  - a worker killed mid-batch leaves entries that a new worker handles;
  - one that always fails ends in the dead-letter record.

issues.title: A desk reply that fails to post is deleted from the mailbox on the next poll and lost
issues.body:
## What happens today

- `desk/inbound.go:162-167`: `claim` commits an `inbound_mail` row with outcome `processing` before any work.
- If posting the comment fails, `Handle` returns an error and `:117-122` leave the mail in the box ("a database or a relay that is down should not lose a reply").
- On the next poll (`ARMATURE_POP3_INTERVAL`, 30 s by default), `claim` (`:290-300`) takes the row again only when `received_at < now() - interval '5 minutes'`. Otherwise it reports not claimed, and `Handle` returns `Duplicate`.
- `:129` then returns `true`, and the POP3 reader sends `DELE`.

**Scenario:** a customer mails a reply during a short database blip. The reply never reaches the request, and the mail is deleted 30 seconds later.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed `Handle` resets or removes its `processing` row, so the next poll handles the mail again.
- [ ] A mail whose row is still `processing` and recent is left in the box (Skipped), never deleted as Duplicate.
- [ ] A mail that keeps failing is given up after a bound and recorded with its error, and agents can see it.

## Tests

- **Integration:** make the comment fail once, poll again, and see the reply posted and the mail deleted only then.

issues.title: A large import trims the event stream past what slower consumers have read, and their events are skipped
issues.body:
## What happens today

- `events/relay.go:38`: `StreamMaxLen = 10_000`.
- `relay.go:155-166`: `XAdd{MaxLen: r.maxLen, Approx: true}` trims by length, whatever the consumer groups have read.
- The relay loops without a pause while batches are full (`:72-80`).
- `issue/import.go:140` emits one `issue.created` per imported issue.

**Scenario:**
1. Import a 15,000-row CSV, and the relay pushes all 15k events in seconds.
2. A group that writes one transaction per event, such as notify or audit, falls more than 10k entries behind.
3. The oldest entries it has not read are trimmed, and `XREADGROUP >` silently skips past them.

Those issues never produce notifications, webhooks or rule runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The relay holds back while the slowest group's lag (`XINFO GROUPS`) is near the cap. Or trimming is by the minimum acknowledged id (`XTRIM MINID`) and not by length.
- [ ] The relay's lag and the groups' lag are exported as metrics, with an alert threshold documented.
- [ ] Nothing is trimmed that some group has not acknowledged.

## Tests

- **Integration:** with a small cap and a slow consumer, push past the cap and see every event handled.

issues.title: A read replica that is down when the api or worker starts is never used until the process restarts
issues.body:
## What happens today

`db/cluster.go:138-149`: when `openPool` fails for a replica, the code logs "the health loop will pick it up when it returns" and `continue`s, so the replica is never added to `c.replicas`. `healthLoop` and `checkAll` (`:256-275`) only go over `c.replicas`, and nothing else adds to it.

**Scenario:** on a fresh `helm install` with cnpg, the `-ro` standbys are still starting while the api pods boot (or a replica restarts during an api rollout). Those pods send every read to the primary for their whole life, and `/readyz` does not show the missing replica.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every configured replica is registered, unhealthy when its pool cannot be opened. The health loop retries opening the pool and brings it into rotation when it answers.
- [ ] `/readyz` (or metrics) lists each replica and whether it is in rotation.

## Tests

- **Integration:** start a cluster with a replica URL that is down, bring the replica up, and see reads reach it.

issues.title: Someone in two organizations rarely or never gets the second organization's digest
issues.body:
## What happens today

- `notify/digest.go:34`: `sent map[uuid.UUID]time.Time` is keyed by user only.
- `due` (`:102-108`) reads `d.sent[userID]`, and `:151` sets it after any organization's bundle.
- `Once` goes through the rows `ORDER BY org_id, user_id` (`:65`).
- A daily digest is due when `now.Hour() == 8 && now.Sub(last) >= time.Hour`.

**Scenario:** a person is in organizations A and B, with a daily digest in both.
1. At 08:00, A's bundle is sent, and `sent[user]` becomes 08:00.
2. B is not due at 08:00, 08:15, 08:30 or 08:45.
3. At 09:00 the hour no longer matches.

B's digest is never mailed, and its `notification_digest` rows pile up. Hourly digests for B are starved the same way whenever A has items every hour.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The sent record is keyed by organization and person, and kept in the database so a restart or a second worker does not resend or skip.
- [ ] A daily digest that missed its hour is sent at the next pass of the day, not skipped.

## Tests

- **Unit:** `due` across two organizations.
- **Integration:** both organizations' digests are mailed in one pass at 08:00.

issues.title: On a database migrated as a plain owner, three backfills reach no organization: default holiday calendar, automation account, Initiative type
issues.body:
## What happens today

`org` forces row level security on its owner (`00001:171`, forced again in `00904:20`). The chart migrates as an owner that is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS, so a migration that reads `FROM org` sees no rows. `00904`'s header documents exactly this for the roles backfill, and fixes only that one. Three more backfills have the same shape:

- `00909_holiday_calendars.sql:25-26`: `INSERT INTO holiday_calendar ... SELECT id, 'Holidays', true FROM org`. Existing organizations get no default calendar, while new ones do (`bootstrap.go:177`).
- `00033_automation.sql:17`: the automation account backfill. `automation/service.go:337-341` then fails with "this organization has no automation account".
- `00005_issue_hierarchy.sql:42-45`: the Initiative type.

`backend/test/owner_migrate_test.go` checks only `org_role`.

**Scenario:** a chart deployment with existing organizations upgrades through 00909. Its organizations have no default holiday calendar, so the plan and the availability pages behave differently from a new organization's.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new migration repeats the three backfills with row security lifted around them, as `00904` does, adding nothing where the rows already exist.
- [ ] `owner_migrate_test.go` asserts the default holiday calendar, the automation account and the Initiative type for an organization made before the migrations ran.
- [ ] A note in the migration guidance (or a lint over `migrations/`) flags `FROM org` in a backfill without `NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the extended owner-migration test.

issues.title: One organization's slow webhook endpoint holds up every other organization's webhooks for up to half an hour
issues.body:
## What happens today

`webhook/webhook.go:496-531`: `SendDue` posts up to 200 deliveries (`sendBatch`, `:492`) one after another, each allowed `sendTimeout = 10s` (`:37`). The worker runs as a single replica.

**Scenario:** organization A's endpoint hangs, with 200 deliveries queued. One pass takes about 33 minutes, and every other organization's deliveries wait behind it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deliveries are posted concurrently by a bounded pool, with at most a few in flight per endpoint.
- [ ] An endpoint that times out repeatedly is backed off on its own, without holding the batch.
- [ ] The pool size is a setting with a documented default.

## Tests

- **Integration:** one endpoint that sleeps and one that answers; the fast one is delivered within a second.

issues.title: With replicas, the invitations list can still show an invitation just withdrawn, or miss one just sent
issues.body:
## What happens today

`auth/tokens_admin.go:39` (`CreateInvite`) and `:129` (`RevokeInvite`) throw away the position `s.db.Write` returns. They have no position to return, so `httpapi/auth_handlers.go:263-290` and `:340-351` never call `NoteWrite`. `ListInvites` (`:73-75`) reads through `s.db.Read`, which goes to a replica. The SPA refetches the list on success (`web/src/api/invites.ts:44,53`).

**Scenario:** an administrator withdraws an invitation, and the refetch hits a replica a second behind. The withdrawn invitation is still listed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both methods return `db.LSN`, and the handlers note it.
- [ ] A check over the services finds other writes whose position is discarded. A test that greps for `_, err = s.db.Write(` in services reached by a handler is enough.

## Tests

- **Integration (with the replica):** withdraw, then list, and the invitation is gone.

issues.title: Keep the api and web available through node drains and rollouts: disruption budgets and a shutdown drain
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want a node drain or a rolling update to drop no requests, so that people do not see 502s every time I deploy.

## What happens today

There is no PodDisruptionBudget, `preStop`, `topologySpreadConstraints` or anti-affinity anywhere in `deploy/charts/armature`. `cmd/api/main.go:276-281` calls `srv.Shutdown` as soon as SIGTERM arrives. `/readyz` never turns unready first, so the listener closes while endpoints are still being removed.

**Scenario:** a node drain evicts both default api replicas, or both web replicas, at once. During a rolling update, requests still routed to a terminating pod get connection refused or 502.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Optional PDBs (`minAvailable: 1`) for api and web, on by default when replicas are more than one.
- [ ] Optional topology spread across nodes.
- [ ] On SIGTERM the api fails `/readyz`, waits a configurable drain delay, then shuts down gracefully. Web gets a `preStop` sleep.
- [ ] The README's deployment section describes them.

## Tests

- **Helm golden files:** updated for each setting.
- **Unit:** the api's shutdown order (readiness off, delay, then Shutdown).

issues.title: ARMATURE_DB_REPLICA_LAG_SAMPLES does nothing, ARMATURE_OIDC_REDIRECT_URL is undocumented, and production starts on localhost defaults
issues.body:
## What happens today

- **Lag samples:** `ARMATURE_DB_REPLICA_LAG_SAMPLES` is read into `config.DB.ReplicaLagSamples` (`config/config.go:66,172`), documented in the README ("samples kept per replica") and set by the chart (`_helpers.tpl:221`, `values.yaml:141`). No code reads it. `db/cluster.go:330-333` takes a replica out on one lag sample over `maxLag`, so replicas flap on a single slow check whatever the setting says.
- **Redirect URL:** `cmd/api/main.go:388-393` reads `ARMATURE_OIDC_REDIRECT_URL`, defaulting to `http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback`. It is missing from the README's table of every variable.
- **Localhost defaults:** `ARMATURE_APP_URL` defaults to `http://localhost:5173` and is used for invite and share links and the write-origin check (`httpapi/edges.go:25`). `config.Load` (`:245-290`) checks neither default when `ARMATURE_ENV` is staging or production.

**Scenario:** a deployment without the chart, with `ARMATURE_ENV=production` and these unset, starts fine. It then sends SSO users to localhost, mails invite links to localhost, and refuses browser writes from the real origin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The lag check keeps the last N samples per replica and acts on their median (or the variable is removed from config, README and chart).
- [ ] `ARMATURE_OIDC_REDIRECT_URL` is in the README table and the chart.
- [ ] Outside development, `config.Load` refuses to start while either URL is a localhost default, with a sentence naming the variable to set.
- [ ] A unit test compares the variables `config` and `main` read with the README table, both ways.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the lag window, the refusal, and the documentation check.

issues.title: The audit log records nothing when webhooks, rules, invitations, role definitions or groups change, or on a password sign-in
issues.body:
## What happens today

- **Webhooks:** `webhook/webhook.go` Create, Update, RotateSecret and Delete emit no event and write no audit entry.
- **Rules:** `automation/service.go` is the same.
- **Invitations:** `auth/tokens_admin.go:24,128` (CreateInvite, RevokeInvite) write no audit.

**Scenario:** an administrator adds a webhook subscribed to `*` that points outside, or redefines the `user` role to include administration. `GET /audit` shows neither.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of these changes is recorded with actor, object and time, through events copied by the audit consumer or through `audit.Record` in the same transaction.
- [ ] Secrets never reach the audit entry: a rotated webhook secret is recorded as rotated.

issues.title: Self-service password recovery by mail
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who forgot my password, I want to reset it from the sign-in page by mail, so that I am not locked out when nobody can reset it for me.

## What happens today

Nothing in the backend or web handles a forgotten password. The only match for the idea is a seeded demo story (`cmd/seed/main.go:367`). An administrator's reset (`SetManagedPassword`) works only for people whose sole organization is the administrator's, as the decisions say. An owner, or someone in two organizations, has no way back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Forgot your password?" on the sign-in page takes an address and always answers the same way, whether or not the address is known.
- [ ] A known address gets a single-use link, valid for an hour, stored hashed. It is rate limited per address and per IP.
- [ ] Using it sets a new password and ends every session and API token the person holds.
- [ ] Accounts that sign in only through a provider are told to use it.
- [ ] Each step is audited, and the decisions record the rule.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - request, use, reuse refused, expired refused;
  - sessions and tokens ended;
  - the same answer for an unknown address.
- **Browser:** reset through Mailpit and sign in.

issues.title: A second factor for password sign-in, and an organization setting that requires it

As the owner of a self-hosted tracker, I want administrators to need a second factor, so that a leaked password alone does not open the organization.

- [ ] An organization can require a second factor for administrators, or for everyone. A session without one is held to enrolment.
- [ ] Single sign-on sessions rely on the provider's factor.
- [ ] Enrolment, removal and recovery-code use are audited, and the decisions record the rule.
- [ ] WebAuthn is noted as later work if not done here.

## Tests

- **Unit:** TOTP verification with clock skew.
- **Integration:** enrolment, sign-in with and without a code, recovery codes single use, and an organization's requirement.

## User story

As an IT administrator, I want people who leave the company removed from Armature when they leave the identity provider, not at their next sign-in, which never comes.

## What happens today

issues.title: A description or comment started in the side panel is saved to the next issue you step to
issues.body:
## What happens today

- `web/src/features/issues/IssuePanel.tsx:23` renders `<IssuePage issueKey={current} inDrawer />` with no `key`.
- `IssuePage.tsx:25` unmounts only while `isLoading`. A cached issue is not loading, so the same subtree is reused for the next issue.
- `Description.tsx:9-13` keeps its `editing` and `draft` state, then calls `update.mutate({ key: issueKey, description: draft })` with the new key.
- `IssueActivity.tsx:79-90` keeps the comment body and posts it to the new key.

**Scenario:**
1. Open A in the panel and press Down to B.
2. Edit B's description and type something.
3. Press Up back to A, which is cached, so no skeleton shows. The editor still holds B's text under A's header.
4. Press Save. A's description is overwritten.

A half-typed comment and Ctrl+Enter behave the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The issue page is keyed by issue in the panel and in `issue-detail.tsx`, so drafts never carry over.
- [ ] Stepping away from an issue with an unsaved draft asks first, or keeps the draft with its own issue.

## Tests

issues.title: Escape in a menu or confirm also closes the drawer or dialog underneath it
issues.body:
## What happens today

`useEscape` (`web/src/components/ui/overlay.ts:11-22`) adds a `document` keydown listener and calls `event.stopPropagation()`, which does not stop other listeners on `document`. Dialog (`Dialog.tsx:30`), Drawer (`:137`) and Menu (`Menu.tsx:44`) each register one, so one press closes every open overlay. The Drawer also ignores `isEditing`, which `DockedPanel` checks (`Dialog.tsx:183-184`).

**Scenario:** on a narrow screen, an issue opens in the Drawer.
- Press Remove on a work log, then Escape in the confirm: the confirm and the issue both close.
- Escape in the issue's header menu, or while typing a comment, closes the drawer and drops the draft.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Escape closes only the topmost overlay. Use a stack in `overlay.ts`, or check and set `defaultPrevented` and use `stopImmediatePropagation`.
- [ ] Focus returns to whatever opened the overlay that closed.
- [ ] The Drawer has the same guard against closing while editing as the docked panel.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** a menu inside a drawer, and a confirm inside a dialog; Escape closes only the top one.
- **Browser:** the work log scenario above.

issues.title: Make the test run faster, the browser suite first
issues.body:
## Request

"optimize the test run, especially the e2e tests so we can develop with more speed create a ticket with the exact request and plan to implement it"

## Where the time goes today (main at 7380763)

| Layer | Time |
|---|---|
| Browser suite (176 scenarios, 4 browsers) | 680s wall; scenarios sum to 2686s; median 13.8s, p90 24.7s, max 39s |
| Integration | about 97s |
| Vitest | 55s; jsdom setup accounts for 139s of the per-worker total |
| Go unit tests | under 2s per package; the time goes to compiling |

The four browsers are evenly loaded (2686s / 4 = 671s), so the run is not waiting on the last scenario to finish. Each scenario is simply slow.

**Browser suite**
- **Page loads.** The suite makes about 1175 full page loads, 6.7 per scenario.
  - Every load goes to the Vite dev server, which transforms and sends about 310 source modules each time. No route is lazy loaded.
  - Each scenario gets a fresh incognito context, so every scenario starts with a cold cache. `e2e/helpers.mjs:13` already blames the dev server for this.
- **Setup through forms.** 691 of those loads (59%) come from setup helpers that fill in forms:

  | Helper | Calls |
  |---|---|
  | `signUp` | 172 |
  | `createProject` | 129 |
  | `createIssue` | 126 |
  | `signIn` | 61 |
  | `signOut` | 32 |
  | invite helpers | the rest |

- **Password hashing.** Every sign-up and sign-in pays a full argon2id hash: 64 MiB, t=3, p=4, at most 4 at once. Compose does not set `ARMATURE_ARGON_*`.
- **Fixed sleeps** add up to only about 15s. The biggest are `board.mjs:269-283` (3.5s in place of a wait) and the 3s loop at `desk-mail.mjs:118`.
- **What already exists to build on:**
  - The setup API routes: `POST /auth/signup`, `/auth/login`, `/projects` and `/projects/{key}/issues`.
  - The production web build: `deploy/Dockerfile.web` target `production`, nginx with `deploy/nginx.conf`, which proxies `/api/` to `api:8080`.
  - `sameSite` (`backend/internal/httpapi/edges.go:23`) accepts a JSON request with no Origin, so node-side setup calls work.

**Integration**
- 339 tests in one package, none of them parallel.
- `newHarness` opens about 5 pools and 8 or more connections in each of 330 tests.
- `newAPIServer` calls `attachmentStore`, which runs `EnsureBucket`, 4 times.
- Go runs top-level parallel tests only after every sequential one has finished. So the tests that pause replication or share the outbox can stay sequential and never overlap the parallel ones.

## Rules for every step

- **One PR per step, each measured.** Each PR's body gives before and after times from the same machine.
- **Green three times running.** `make test-all` passes, and the full browser suite passes three runs in a row. A speed-up that adds a flake is not done.
- **Forms stay tested.** A scenario whose subject is a form (sign-up, sign-in, project creation, issue creation, accepting an invite) still drives that form. Only scenarios that need the result as a precondition get it through the API.

## Plan

**1. Measure.** `e2e/runner.mjs`
- The runner writes `.cache/e2e/timings.json`: per scenario, its time and how many page loads it made. `goto` and `reload` count them.
- At the end of a run it prints the 10 slowest scenarios.
- `ONLY` also matches the scenario file name, as in `ONLY=board`. `suite.mjs` records which module registered each scenario.

**2. Set up through the API.** `e2e/helpers.mjs` and the scenarios
- `signUp`, `signIn`, `createProject`, `createIssue`, `acceptInvite` and `dashboardFixture` make their calls from node, as JSON `fetch` requests against `BASE_URL`.
- They copy the session cookie into the scenario's context with `page.setCookie`.
- They take `{ visit }`, default true, which loads the page the form version ended on, so scenarios keep working unchanged. Chained setup passes `visit: false` to every call but the last.
- The form versions stay as `signUpThroughForm`, `createProjectThroughForm` and so on. The scenarios in `accounts`, `projects`, `work` and `invitations` whose subject they are keep using them.

**3. Serve the production build to the browser suite.** `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `Makefile`
- New compose service `web-e2e`, built from `Dockerfile.web` target `production` under profile `e2e`, so `make up` is unchanged.
- `make test-e2e` and `make screenshots` first run `docker compose --profile e2e up -d --build web-e2e`. Layer caching makes that a no-op when `web/` is unchanged.
- The suite then runs with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://web-e2e`. Setting `E2E_WEB=dev` keeps the dev server, for debugging a scenario with hot reload.
- The suite now also tests what ships. If nginx's CSP blocks something, such as a library that injects a `<style>` element, that is a production bug and is fixed in this PR.
- Lower `LOAD_WAIT` and fix its comment once the numbers show the dev server's slack is no longer needed.

**4. Cheaper password hashing on the dev stack.** `deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- Set `ARMATURE_ARGON_MEMORY_KIB=8192`, `ARMATURE_ARGON_ITERATIONS=1` and `ARMATURE_ARGON_THREADS=1` on `api`, the same as the seed and the integration harness.
- Helm and the production defaults keep the OWASP parameters. A comment says why the dev stack differs.

**5. Replace fixed sleeps with waits.**
- `board.mjs:264-283`: wait for the swimlane save, and drop the `waitForFunction(... || true)` that never waits.
- `desk-mail.mjs:118`: poll every 250ms instead of sleeping 3s.
- `board.mjs:132`: wait for a condition instead of sleeping 300ms.

**6. More browsers, longest first.** `e2e/runner.mjs`
- Order the queue by the previous `timings.json`, longest first, so the tail stays short as more workers are added.
- Run the full suite with `WORKERS` at 4, 6 and 8. Set `DEFAULT_WORKERS` to the fastest count that stays green three times.
- Check that the throttles keyed by IP hold up at that parallelism: PDF renders (6 per minute) and invalid invite attempts (10 per 10 minutes).

**7. Integration: one harness for the whole package.** `backend/test/harness_test.go`, `apiclient_test.go`
- A `TestMain` opens the cluster, the superuser and replica pools, the telemetry exporter and one attachment store, once. `newHarness` hands them out.
- The every-operation coverage check moves from `zz_coverage_test.go` into `TestMain`, after `m.Run`.

**8. Integration: parallel tests.**
- Tests scoped to one organization call `t.Parallel()`.
- These stay sequential, which in Go means they finish before any parallel test starts:
  - replication pause and lag, and replica join;
  - outbox, relay and consumer;
  - the session wipe in `security_test.go`;
  - the throttle tests.
- A guard test, in the style of `kept_positions_test.go`, refuses a new top-level test that neither calls `t.Parallel()` nor is on the sequential list with its reason.
- Pool sizes stay within Postgres `max_connections`, counting the api and worker.

**9. Vitest.** `web/vite.config.ts`
- Try `pool: "threads"`, and drop the Tailwind plugin under Vitest.
- Keep each change only if it is faster and green three times.
- jsdom stays; happy-dom would trade fidelity for speed.

**10. `make test-all` runs what it can side by side.** `Makefile`
- Unit tests, vitest (in a target of its own) and integration run side by side with `$(MAKE) -j3 --output-sync=target`. The browser suite follows once they pass.
- Integration and the browser suite never overlap: integration stops the worker and pauses the shared replica.

## Targets

| Layer | Now | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Browser suite, default settings | 680s | 300s or less |
| One scenario with `ONLY`, web build unchanged | (to measure in step 1) | under 20s |
| Integration | 97s | 45s or less |
| Vitest | 55s | 40s or less |
| `make test-all` | about 15 min | under 7 min |

## Left out, and why

- **Waking the outbox relay with LISTEN/NOTIFY.** It saves up to 1s on about 12 waits. Revisit after step 6.
- **Relaxing Postgres durability** (`synchronous_commit` or `fsync` off). It changes replica lag, which the integration suite asserts on.
- **happy-dom.** It is less faithful than jsdom.
- **CI sharding.** No CI workflow runs the tests today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every step above is either merged with its before and after numbers, or closed with the measurement that showed it did not help.
- [ ] The targets table is met on this machine, or the issue says which target was missed and why.
- [ ] `make test-all` and three consecutive full browser runs are green on main afterwards.
- [ ] Each form named under "Rules for every step" is still driven through the UI by at least one scenario.

issues.title: Show the Armature logo and give the tab a favicon
issues.body:
Armature has no visual identity in the browser: the tab shows the browser's blank page icon, and the places that name the product (the sign-in and sign-up door, the "not in an organization" page, the header of a shared dashboard) print a plain monospace \`armature\`.

There is now a logo (the gopher winding the armature, on a dark blue field).

## What to do

- Give the SPA a favicon and an Apple touch icon cut from the logo's emblem, so a tab or a home-screen shortcut is recognisable at a glance.
- Put the emblem beside the \`armature\` wordmark wherever the wordmark appears today, through one component so the three places cannot drift apart.
- Ship the images as static files from \`web/public\` so the production nginx image serves them unchanged.

## Done when

- The browser tab shows the emblem in development and in the production image.
- The sign-in, sign-up, no-organization and shared dashboard pages show the emblem next to the wordmark, in light and dark theme.

issues.title: Load test the API with k6 to know what one deployment can carry
issues.body:
Nothing today says how much load Armature can take. The four test layers prove that it behaves correctly, and #187 makes them faster, but none of them puts concurrent users on the stack. The repository has no k6 scripts and no Go benchmarks. So we cannot say how many people one api replica serves, where latency starts to climb, or whether a change made it slower.

## What to do

- Add k6 scenarios under `perf/` that act like real use, signing in through the same session cookie the SPA uses:
  - Opening a board and moving cards between columns
  - Searching with NQL, paging the project's issue list, and the CSV export
  - Opening an issue, commenting, and changing a field or status (workflow transitions)
  - Service desk: the portal raising a request, and agents reading their queues
  - Incoming git and CI webhooks
- Add a `make test-perf` target that runs the `grafana/k6` image on `armature_default` against the running stack, the same way `make test-e2e` runs Chromium. Nothing gets installed on the host. `SCENARIO=` and `VUS=`/`DURATION=` choose what runs and how hard.
- Load a data set big enough to matter (many projects, tens of thousands of issues, long histories). Either extend `cmd/seed` or add a separate perf seed, so the numbers do not come from a near-empty database.
- Write thresholds per scenario (p95 latency, error rate) into the scripts, so a run that gets worse fails instead of only printing numbers.
- Read the run against what is already there: the Prometheus metrics, `make observe` traces, `make stack-stats`, and replica lag (`ARMATURE_DB_MAX_REPLICA_LAG`), to find out whether the api, Postgres, Redis or the worker gives out first.

## Done when

- `make test-perf` runs every scenario against a seeded stack and fails when a threshold is crossed.
- The README's Testing section explains how to run it and lists the baseline numbers from a first run, along with the machine they came from.
- What the first runs find (slow queries, missing indexes, N+1 reads) is filed as separate issues.

## Not in scope

- Running it on every commit. It is a manual or nightly check until the numbers are stable enough to gate on.
- Load testing the production cluster.

issues.title: Remove organizations: one installation is one team's tracker
issues.body:
## Why

Armature is self-hosted, and an installation serves one team. Organizations add a layer that such an installation never uses:
- founding an organization at sign-up, then choosing and switching between them;
- slugs in single sign-on and desk addresses;
- rules for people who belong to several organizations;
- one setting per organization for things that are really one setting.

This epic removes organizations from everything people and the API see, then from the schema.

## Decisions

1. **Product first, schema later.** The product and API lose organizations first, while one organization row stays inside, so `org_id` and row security keep working. The last ticket drops the columns, once the product works without organizations.
2. **Upgrading with several organizations is refused.** The upgrade migration stops with a message naming the organizations, until only one remains. There is no automatic merge: project keys, statuses, roles and people would collide.
3. **Accounts.** On an empty installation, the first sign-up becomes its administrator. After that people come in by invitation, by single sign-on, by an administrator creating them, or, with `ARMATURE_SIGNUP=open`, by signing up as plain members.
4. **Browser suite isolation.** The browser suite isolates scenarios by unique names and project keys. A serial lane holds the scenarios that change installation-wide settings, the same pattern as the integration suite's sequential list.

**What stays, under plainer names:**
- the audit log, groups, roles, global fields, workflows and schemes, labels, holiday calendars, rules and webhooks;
- the permission key `org.administer`. Its label becomes "Administer Armature".

## Order

- [x] #209 The browser suite isolates scenarios without an organization each. This comes first.
- [x] #210 One installation: the organization is created at install, and an upgrade with several is refused.
- [x] #211 Accounts without organizations: sign-up, invitations, members, owners.
- [x] #212 Sign-in without organizations: no switching, one identity provider, one second-factor rule.
- [x] #213 Delete organization lifecycle: creating, demo organizations, deleting.
- [x] #214 The service desk without an organization slug.
- [x] #215 Say "everyone" instead of "the organization" in the product and the API.
- [x] #216 Docs, seed and deployment for one installation.
- [x] #217 The integration suite isolates tests without an organization each.
- [x] #218 Drop `org_id` and the tenant layer from the schema.

#214 depends only on #210 and can run beside #211 to #213. Every ticket keeps all four test layers green.

## Out of scope

- Merging the data of several organizations.
- Running more than one team on one installation; that takes separate installations.

issues.title: The browser suite isolates scenarios without an organization each
issues.body:
## User story

As someone removing organizations from Armature (epic #208), I want the browser suite to keep its scenarios apart without each one signing up an organization of its own. Then every later step can land without breaking the suite.

## What happens today

- 182 of 185 scenarios start with `signUp` (`e2e/helpers.mjs:223-237`), which posts `/auth/signup` with `orgName`. Each scenario becomes the owner of an empty organization, and that organization is its sandbox. `README.md:245-247` and `e2e/runner.mjs:62-63` say so.
- Project keys come from the project name and are unique only within an organization. "Helpdesk" (HELP) is created 9 times, and "Tracked", "Read only", "Moving", "IT desk" and "Drawn" twice each.
- About ten scenarios change settings that would be installation-wide once organizations are gone. In one shared installation they would break the scenarios running beside them:
  - `accounts.mjs:240` requires a second factor for everyone, which holds every other session.
  - `themes.mjs:152` sets the default theme.
  - `dashboards.mjs:44-78` and `workflows.mjs:182-272` change the default workflow.
  - `access.mjs:148,241` sets the single sign-on provider and adds a role.
  - `holidays.mjs:38,72` sets the default calendar.
  - `organization.mjs:130` adds a field to every project.
  - `issue-details.mjs:258` renames a global label.
  - `work.mjs:110` adds a webhook that hears every event.
- The runner (`e2e/runner.mjs:65-99`) has a single queue shared by four browsers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **One administrator per run.** A run sets up the installation's administrator once: by the first sign-up on an empty stack, or by signing in when it already exists. The helpers know its credentials.
- [ ] **`signUp` makes a new person.** The administrator creates the account (`POST /users`) with the role the scenario asks for, and the scenario signs in as it. Scenarios that administer something ask for an administrator explicitly.
- [ ] **Unique project keys.** `createProject` always passes a unique key, and scenarios read the key back rather than assume it.
- [ ] **A serial lane.** `serialScenario(name, fn)` registers a scenario that runs after the parallel pool, with one browser. Every scenario listed above is serial and puts back what it changed.
- [ ] **A guard.** A scenario that changes an installation-wide setting from the parallel pool is refused, by a check like `backend/test/parallel_test.go`'s or by a reviewed list that the runner enforces.
- [ ] **Docs.** README "Testing" and CLAUDE.md say how a scenario stays isolated.
- [ ] This lands before the sign-up change, and works both with organizations (today) and without them.

## Tests

- Two full runs in a row on the same stack, both green.
- One run with the parallel pool shuffled, to show no scenario depends on another.

Depends on: nothing. This is the first step.

issues.title: One installation: the organization is created at install, and an upgrade with several is refused
issues.body:
## User story

As the operator of an Armature installation, I want it to be one tracker with one set of people and settings, created when it is installed. Then nobody has to found an organization before they can work.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- Every sign-up creates an organization (`auth.Signup`, `backend/internal/auth/service.go:61-208`, bootstrapped by `bootstrap.Org` at `backend/internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:73`). One installation can therefore hold any number of organizations.
- Installation-wide settings live on the `org` row: `default_theme_id` (00902), `second_factor` (00928), `automation_user_id` (00033) and the unused `settings`.
- A person can be signed in with no organization at all:
  - `passwordPrincipal` leaves `Org` nil (`backend/internal/auth/login.go:95-120`);
  - `requireOrg` then answers `no_organization` (`backend/internal/httpapi/middleware.go:438-453`);
  - every `require*Perm` repeats `p.InOrg()`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Upgrade guard.** A migration refuses to run when `org` holds more than one row. Its message names the organizations and says to delete the extra ones with the previous release first. There is no automatic merge, and the CHANGELOG has an upgrade note.
- [ ] **One organization at first start.** An empty installation gets its organization through `bootstrap.Org`, named by `ARMATURE_NAME` (default "Armature"). It is documented in the README variables table, which `config/documented_test.go` checks. Sign-up no longer creates an organization.
- [ ] **`installation` service.** A new `installation` service reads and writes the name and the settings now on `org`. Every installation-wide setting goes through it.
- [ ] **Everyone is in it.** Every signed-in principal is in the installation's organization.
  - `requireOrg`, the `no_organization` error, the `InOrg()` checks and the nil-organization paths go.
  - Someone without a membership cannot sign in. They are told "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator."
- [ ] **Tenant plumbing unchanged.** The backend still carries the tenant per session and per event, so `org_id` and row security keep working. The integration harness may still create extra organizations for isolation until the integration-suite ticket.
- [ ] **Decisions.** `docs/decisions.md` records the rule.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - the migration refuses two organizations and passes with one or none;
  - a first start creates exactly one;
  - a principal always has the organization;
  - someone without a membership is refused with the sentence.

Depends on: #209.

issues.title: Accounts without organizations: sign-up, invitations, members, owners
issues.body:
## User story

As the administrator of an Armature installation, I want accounts to belong to the installation. I set it up with the first sign-up and let people in by invitation, single sign-on or by creating them. No organization name to make up, no "member of another organization" rules.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Sign-up** asks for `orgName` and `orgSlug` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:78-122`; `web/src/features/auth/AuthForms.tsx:264,304-314`; "Create your organization" at `web/src/routes/auth.tsx:97-98`). `SignupPolicy` (`backend/internal/auth/signup.go`) means "the first organization" or "any organization".
- **Invitations** name the organization, and they have a path for someone who already belongs to another one (`backend/internal/auth/tokens_admin.go:173-311`, `web/src/routes/invite.tsx:67-168`).
- **Removing a member** (`privacy.RemoveMember`, `DELETE /members/{id}`) keeps the account for the person's other organizations (`web/src/features/access/MemberList.tsx`).
- **Administrators manage only some accounts:** those that belong to no other organization (`managedSelectSQL.onlyHere`, `ErrManagedElsewhere`, `guardManaged` in `backend/internal/auth/manage.go:96-191`). `CreateLocalUser` refuses an address known elsewhere.
- **Organization-bound rules:**
  - An organization cannot lose its last owner (`soleActiveOwnerOf`, the trigger `app_user_keeps_an_owner` in 00049).
  - API tokens are bound to one organization (`backend/internal/auth/model.go:107-112`).
  - Avatars are visible only within a shared organization (`SharesOrganization`, `backend/internal/auth/profile.go:92`).
  - Account-level acts write one audit entry per organization (`auditEveryOrg`, `backend/internal/auth/recovery.go:154`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Sign-up asks only for the person.** There is no organization name or slug.
  - On an empty installation, the first account becomes owner and administrator.
  - After that, `ARMATURE_SIGNUP` decides: `first` (the default) closes sign-up, `open` lets people sign up as plain members, and `closed` closes it.
  - The README row and the Helm values are updated.
- [ ] **Invitations** invite into the installation. The invitation page and mail name the installation, and the "already in another organization" path goes.
- [ ] **Removing a member switches the account off.** It uses the existing deactivation. "Remove from organization" goes.
- [ ] **Administrators manage every local account.** The sole-organization rules and their errors go.
- [ ] **Last owner becomes last active administrator.** The installation keeps at least one active administrator, in both the service and the trigger.
- [ ] **API tokens are the person's.** The "bound to one organization" wording goes.
- [ ] **Avatars are visible to everyone signed in.**
- [ ] **Account-level audit entries are written once.**
- [ ] **Decisions.** `docs/decisions.md` supersedes "An administrator makes a local user, and manages only what is theirs" and "The owner always administers their own organization".

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - the first account becomes administrator, and the next follows the policy;
  - an invitation is accepted;
  - removing switches the account off;
  - the last administrator cannot be switched off, also checked straight through SQL;
  - an administrator manages any local account.
- **Vitest:** the sign-up form without an organization field.
- **Browser:**
  - sign-up on an empty stack (serial);
  - invite and accept.

Depends on: #209, #210.

issues.title: Sign-in without organizations: no switching, one identity provider, one second-factor rule
issues.body:
## User story

As someone signing in to Armature, I want to land straight in it. No organization to choose, no organization to type for single sign-on, and no switcher.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Organization switching:**
  - `POST /auth/switch-org` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:204-228`, `auth.SwitchOrg` at `backend/internal/auth/service.go:437-472`) moves a session between organizations. It is allowed even while a session is held for second-factor setup (`backend/internal/httpapi/second_factor_handlers.go:50`).
  - After signing in, someone in several organizations is asked which one (`OrganizationChoice`, `web/src/features/auth/AuthForms.tsx:35-62,110-130`). Someone in none sees `web/src/features/shell/NoOrganization.tsx`.
  - The sidebar has an organization switcher (`web/src/features/shell/Sidebar.tsx:88-123`), and the profile lists organizations (`web/src/routes/profile.tsx:168-178`). `/auth/me` returns `organizations`.
- **Sessions and reach:**
  - Sessions record `current_org_id` and `proof_org_id`. `session_reaches` and `session_stays_home` (migration 00905) decide which organizations a single sign-on session reaches.
  - The session principal trusts other organizations with the same issuer (`backend/internal/auth/service.go:231-234`). `ErrSessionStaysHome` and `session_bound` (`backend/internal/httpapi/privacy_handlers.go:25-48`) refuse acts outside the session's organization.
- **Single sign-on** starts at `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start`, and the login form asks for the organization (`AuthForms.tsx:132-185`). Each organization has its own provider.
- **The second-factor rule** lives at `/organization/second-factor` (`backend/internal/auth/secondfactor.go:302-330`). A held session is offered "Go to {org}" (`web/src/features/auth/SecondFactor.tsx:301-330`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Switching goes.** `POST /auth/switch-org`, `OrganizationChoice`, `NoOrganization`, the sidebar switcher, the profile's organizations section, and `organizations`/`Membership` on `/auth/me` are deleted. The sidebar header shows the installation's name.
- [ ] **Sessions forget organizations.** Sessions no longer write `current_org_id` or `proof_org_id`. `session_reaches`, `session_stays_home`, the cross-organization issuer trust, `ErrSessionStaysHome` and `session_bound` go. The session's proof stays.
- [ ] **One identity provider:**
  - Sign-in starts at `/auth/oidc/start`.
  - `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start` redirects there for one release.
  - The login form offers "Continue with single sign-on" without an organization field.
  - Provider settings show the new address.
- [ ] **The second-factor rule moves to `/settings/second-factor`.** It reads "for administrators" or "for everyone", and the "another organization" offers and messages go.
- [ ] **Docs.** `make openapi` is regenerated. `docs/decisions.md` supersedes "A sign-in reaches what its proof vouches for", and SECURITY.md's Session provenance row is updated.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - sign-in lands in the installation;
  - single sign-on starts at the new address, and the old one redirects;
  - the second-factor rule works at its new path;
  - a held session can still sign out and enrol.
- **Vitest:** login without a choice; the sidebar without a switcher.
- **Browser:** the accounts, access and invitations scenarios.

Depends on: #210, #211.

issues.title: Delete organization lifecycle: creating, demo organizations, deleting
issues.body:
## User story

As the administrator of an Armature installation, I want no buttons that make or delete organizations. There is one installation, and its settings page is about that installation.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Demo organizations.** `POST /organizations/demo` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:230-264`) makes a demo organization and switches into it, through `auth.CreateOrganization` (`backend/internal/auth/service.go:392-435`) and `demo.Factory` (`backend/internal/demo/factory.go`).

- **The `org.created` event.** `TopicOrgCreated` (`backend/internal/events/events.go:25,62`) announces new organizations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **The organization endpoints go.** `POST /organizations/demo`, `auth.CreateOrganization`, `DELETE /organization`, `privacy.DeleteOrganization` and `TopicOrgCreated` are deleted.
- [ ] **The demo stays available.** `demo.Factory` stays for the seed. An administrator action "Add the demo project" loads it into the installation.
- [ ] **An Installation page.** The organization settings page becomes "Installation", which shows and renames the installation's name and nothing about creating or deleting.
- [ ] **Organization-lifecycle tests go:**
  - browser: `e2e/scenarios/organization-delete.mjs`, `organization.mjs:162`, `invitations.mjs:114`, `projects.mjs:170`;
  - integration: `organization_delete_test.go`, `demo_test.go`, `TestOrgSwitching`;
  - the takeover and single-sign-on-reach tests are rewritten for one installation.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/privacy.md` loses "An organization letting a member go" and organization deletion. `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the Installation page.
- **Browser:** renaming the installation shows in the sidebar (serial).

Depends on: #210, #212.

issues.title: The service desk without an organization slug
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer of a service desk, I want the desk's address to name the desk, not an organization slug I have never heard of.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Desk addresses.** The public desk lives at `/desk/{orgSlug}`, with `/desk/{orgSlug}/codes` and `/desk/{orgSlug}/sessions` (`backend/internal/httpapi/router.go:62-64`, `deskBySlug` at `backend/internal/httpapi/portal_entry_handlers.go:185-195`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **The web follows.** The web route and the address shown to agents use the new form.
- [ ] **Portal codes and doors.** Codes and open doors no longer carry the organization.
- [ ] **Customer-facing text.** Code mail, the satisfaction page and the portal header name the installation or the desk.
- [ ] **Inbound mail.** The "ambiguous across organizations" outcome goes.
- [ ] **OpenAPI.** `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

  - desk entry, code and session at the new address, and the redirect from the old one;

issues.title: Say "everyone" instead of "the organization" in the product and the API
issues.body:
## User story

As someone using Armature, I want the words on screen to match what there is: settings that apply to every project, not to an "organization" I never chose.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **UI strings.** About 87 strings in 72 files under `web/src` say "organization". Most of them mean "all projects" or "everyone", for example:
  - "Follow the organization" (`web/src/features/workflows/ProjectWorkflows.tsx`, `web/src/features/arrange/ArrangementEditor.tsx:76`)
  - "Share with the organization" (`web/src/routes/themes.tsx`)
  - "Only over the whole organization" (`web/src/features/access/RoleMatrix.tsx`)
  - "Rules across every project of {org}" (`web/src/routes/automation.tsx:56`)
- **Guide and permission label.** The guide catalogue (`web/src/features/guide/catalogue.ts:81-116`) and the permission label "Administer the organization" (`backend/internal/perm/definitions.go:85`) use the same word.
- **OpenAPI.** It has an "organization" tag and summaries (`backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go`).
- **Theme source.** The theme source value `"organization"` (`web/src/api/themes.ts:29`, `backend/internal/theme/service.go:78`) names where a default theme comes from.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **UI copy and help** say "everyone", "all projects" or "Armature", whichever fits each place. The only exception is the Installation page.
- [ ] **The permission label** reads "Administer Armature". Its key `org.administer` stays, because stored role grants use it.

issues.title: Drop org_id and the tenant layer from the schema
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Armature, I want the schema and the code to stop carrying an organization that is always the same. Then queries, triggers and new features no longer pay for multi-tenancy.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Schema:**
  - 94 of 101 tables carry `org_id`.
  - Each has a `_tenant_isolation` and an `_admin_bypass` policy (190 in total), under forced row security. Every policy is pure tenant isolation; project walls, portal scoping and customer rules live in Go and in triggers.
  - About 30 unique indexes and primary keys include `org_id`, for example `project (org_id, key)`. So do the `absence_no_overlap` exclusion and the `role_assignment` to `org_role` foreign key.
  - 36 trigger functions refer to the organization. Some mix tenant checks with project, customer or owner rules that must stay: `issue_sprint_guard`, `team_member_guard`, `absence_guard`, `saved_filter_share_guard`, `role_assignment_guard`, `app_user_keeps_an_owner` and others.
- **Go:**
  - `internal/tenant`, `db.inTx`'s `set_config('app.org_id')` and `ErrNoTenant`.
  - About 129 INSERT column lists with `org_id`, 93 `current_org_id()` uses, 17 `ON CONFLICT (org_id, ...)` clauses and 46 explicit `org_id` filters.
  - 8 worker loops run once per organization: retention, sprint and flow snapshots, digest, subscriptions, SLA watch, automation schedules, webhooks.
  - `events.Event.OrgID` and the Redis stream field; webhook payloads carry `orgId`.
- **Tables:** `org`, `org_member` and `org_role` hold what becomes installation settings and per-person roles.

## Acceptance criteria

The work goes in this order, because Postgres drops dependent objects silently: dropping a column drops its indexes and policies, and trigger bodies fail only at runtime.

- [ ] **1. Policies.** Decide whether any row security remains, for example project walls, and record it in `docs/decisions.md`. Replace or drop the tenant policies, the admin bypass policies and FORCE. Rewrite `rls_bypass_test`, `backfill_rls_test` and `owner_migrate_test`.
- [ ] **2. Constraints.** Recreate every unique index, primary key, exclusion and foreign key that includes `org_id` without it, before the column goes. Project keys become globally unique.
- [ ] **3. Triggers.** Rewrite all 36 trigger functions. Keep their project, customer and owner rules, and drop the "cannot cross organizations" parts.
- [ ] **4. Go.** Remove `org_id` from inserts, conflicts and filters. Delete `internal/tenant` and the tenant setting. Run the worker loops once. Remove `Event.OrgID` and the stream field. Drop `orgId` from webhook payloads; this is a documented contract change, so the CHANGELOG says so.
- [ ] **5. Tables.** `org` becomes an `installation` settings row, `org_member` becomes a role on `app_user`, and `org_role` becomes `role`. Decide whether the `armature_admin` role split stays.
- [ ] **6. Upgrade.** The upgrade note says to drain the outbox and the event stream before migrating.

## Tests

- The full suite on all four layers.
- A migration test that starts from a populated one-organization database and checks every row survives.
- A check that no table, column or function mentions `org_id` or `current_org_id`.

issues.title: Report the build at GET /api/v1/meta, as all three tools do
issues.body:
All three tools answer the same unauthenticated endpoint, so a partner, an operator or Dynamo can tell which build it talks to:

```
GET /api/v1/meta
{
  "product": "stator" | "armature" | "exciter",
  "build": { "version": "1.3.0", "commit": "abc1234", "builtAt": "2026-10-14T09:00:00Z" },
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "capabilities": []
}
```

- `version` is the semver from `VERSION` (a dev build says so, e.g. `1.3.0+4.gabc1234`), `commit` the short git hash, both stamped at build time.
- `apiVersion` is `info.version` of the OpenAPI document; it rises only for a change that breaks clients.
- `capabilities` is filled by the capability issue; until then it is an empty list.
- The endpoint is in the OpenAPI document and covered by a test that compares it with the build stamp.

**Here today:** `GET /api/v1/build` returns `{build: {version, commit, builtAt}}`. Add `/api/v1/meta` in the shape above and keep `/build` working, marked deprecated, for at least one Dynamo release.

issues.title: Release by tag the same way in all three tools
issues.body:
All three tools release the same way, following the release script of [chaosflix-jellyfin](https://github.com/praetorianer777/chaosflix-jellyfin/blob/main/release.sh) and its tag workflow:

- `./release.sh [version] [--dry-run]` infers the next semver from the Conventional Commits since the last tag (breaking: MAJOR, below 1.0.0 MINOR; `feat`: MINOR; `fix` and the rest: PATCH), or takes it by hand, and prints the rule it applied.
- It refuses a checkout that is behind its upstream or not on the default branch, so it never tags code the remote lacks.
- It writes the version into every file that carries one (`VERSION`, `web/package.json` where present, `Chart.yaml` `version` and `appVersion`), adds the CHANGELOG section and makes an annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` whose message is the release notes. A test refuses these files disagreeing.
- Main takes no direct commits here, so the bump travels on a branch `release/vX.Y.Z` with its own pull request; the tag is set on the merge commit (by the script after the merge, or by the workflow), never on a commit main does not have.
- On the tag, CI builds every image from the tag, pushes it to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<tool>-<image>:X.Y.Z` (and the commit hash), packages and publishes the chart, publishes the GitHub release from the tag message, and sends a `repository_dispatch` to Dynamo with the tool and version.
- A build not made from a tag says so in its version (`X.Y.Z+N.g<hash>`), so a dev image is never mistaken for a release.

**Here today:** `make release VERSION=x.y.z` (`deploy/release.sh`) already bumps every file on a `release/` branch and a test holds them together; keep that, and add the version inference from the commit history (needs the branch and commit convention issue), the tag workflow on GitHub (only the Jenkinsfile builds images today) and the Dynamo dispatch.

issues.title: Give the webhook envelope a version
issues.body:
The webhook envelope carries a version, so its format can change without breaking receivers silently:

```
{ "version": 1, "id": "...", "topic": "issue.updated", "occurredAt": "...", "payload": { ... } }
```

- `version` is an integer and rises only for a change that breaks receivers (a field removed, renamed or changing meaning). Adding a field or a topic does not raise it.
- It is also sent as a header `X-<Product>-Webhook-Version`, so a receiver can decide before parsing.
- A sender of version N+1 keeps sending N to endpoints that registered for N, for at least one Dynamo release.
- A receiver ignores unknown fields and topics, and refuses an envelope version it does not know with a clear status and log line, instead of misreading it.
- The format is described in the OpenAPI document (or a JSON schema next to it) and covered by a contract test on both sides.

**Here:** Armature is the sender; the envelope is `{id, topic, orgId, occurredAt, payload}` (`backend/internal/webhook/webhook.go`), with no version. Add it, and let an endpoint record the version it was registered for. Note: Stator no longer reads `orgId` (one organization per instance).

## What happens

The browser scenario "a project's sidebar links to its documentation" fails now and then (twice in a row on one branch, once on another, and alone with ONLY): the last save, which clears the link, never reaches the api.

Two things meet there:

issues.title: Dialogs and popovers taller than the screen cannot be scrolled, so their buttons are out of reach
issues.body:
## What happens

When a dialog is taller than the window, its lower part cannot be reached. With the built-in arrangement, the new issue dialog asks for about fifteen fields plus every custom field, so on a laptop screen the footer with "Create issue" sits below the window and nothing scrolls.

**Why:**
- In `web/src/components/ui/Dialog.tsx:35-45`, the backdrop is `fixed inset-0 ... items-start pt-[12vh]`. It has no `overflow-y-auto`, and the panel has no `max-h`.
- `useScrollLock` (`web/src/components/ui/overlay.ts:107-117`) sets `body { overflow: hidden }` while a dialog is open.
- A fixed box is not a scroll container, so the overflow is simply lost. Tab cannot reach the hidden controls either.

The browser suite never noticed, because `clickButton` (`e2e/helpers.mjs:754-764`) clicks through the DOM and works on buttons outside the viewport.

**Dialogs that grow past the screen in the same way:**
- the new issue dialog (`features/issues/CreateIssueDialog.tsx`);
- the automation rule editor, one block per condition and action (`features/automation/RuleEditor.tsx`);
- the bulk edit result, one row per refused issue, up to 200 (`features/filters/BulkBar.tsx:107`);
- a project's status history, every update ever posted (`features/projects/StatusStrip.tsx:117`);
- the export columns, the dashboard share links, the absence editor, and the move dialog.

**Menus and popovers:**
- `Menu` (`components/ui/Menu.tsx:104`) and `Popover` (`components/ui/Popover.tsx:41`) have no height limit.
- `useAnchored` (`overlay.ts:126-178`) clamps the position to the viewport but never the height.
- **Affected:** the sidebar project switcher, which holds 20 projects and a filter box, so its last projects are cut off on a 768px screen. Also the fix-version, affects-version and component pickers (`features/versions/IssueVersionFields.tsx:49`), the board's quick filters (`features/board/QuickFilters.tsx:149`), the resource grid's week popover (`features/resources/ResourceGrid.tsx:114`), and the canned responses menu (`features/issues/IssueActivity.tsx:201`).

**Errors out of view:** the create dialog (`CreateIssueDialog.tsx:109-110`) and the rule editor (`RuleEditor.tsx:80`) show their error at the top of the body, while the button that caused it is in the footer. Once the body scrolls, pressing Create seems to do nothing.

issues.title: Let a person ask for access to an issue they may not see, without telling whether it exists
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter show Armature issues on their pages with each reader's own token. A reader who may not see an issue gets 404, the same answer as for an issue that does not exist, so the page can only say "you may not see PROJ-12, or it does not exist". People take that for a fault. (Stator: praetorianer777/Stator#426.)

Armature treats existence as privileged (`httpapi/errors.go`, `scope.go`), and that should stay the default. Two ways to help the reader without weakening it:

**1. Ask for access, without learning anything (recommended)**
- `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/access-requests` with an optional message. It always answers `202 Accepted` with the same body, whether the issue exists, the caller may already see it, or the project is hidden from them; so it reveals nothing.
- When the issue exists and the caller may not see it, the project's administrators get a notification (in Armature and by mail) naming the caller, the key and the message, with a one-click way to grant access to the issue's project. Repeated requests by one person for one project within a day are folded into one.
- Rate limited per caller.
- Partners link to it: Stator's "You may not see PROJ-12, or it no longer exists. Ask for access" calls it with the reader's token.
- Capability `issue.access-requests@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.

**2. Optionally say "restricted" for projects that allow it**
- A per-project setting, off by default: "Show that issues exist to people who may not see them". When on, a caller who may not see an issue of that project gets `403` with code `not_permitted` and the project's name, instead of `404`.
- Only the project's administrators can turn it on; the settings page says what it reveals. Projects that must stay hidden keep the 404.

Both covered by tests that a caller cannot tell apart an existing hidden issue from a missing one unless the project opted in.

issues.title: Let partner tools get a person's token in one click, with consent
issues.body:
Stator and Exciter call Armature as each person, with a personal access token the person makes in Armature and pastes into the other tool. Many people give up at that step. A partner should be able to get that token in one click, with the person's consent.

- Armature acts as an OAuth 2.0 authorization server for partner tools: authorization code flow with PKCE, refresh tokens, revocation (RFC 7009).
- Clients are registered by an Armature administrator (name, redirect URIs, allowed scopes), or by the partner during the administrator's connect step (see the webhook issue); a registered client shows its name on the consent page.
- Consent page: "**Stator** wants to read issues and link pages as **<person>**: [Allow] [Cancel]", listing the scopes in words.
- Scopes map to what a personal access token can do today (read, issue.write, issue.transition, comment.write, remote links), and the issued token never exceeds the person's own rights.
- Issued tokens appear in the person's token list as "Stator (connected app)", revocable there; revoking ends the refresh token too.
- Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and the capability `oauth.partner-tokens@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.
- With a shared Keycloak realm, Armature accepts Keycloak token exchange (RFC 8693) for a partner client as an alternative, so a signed-in person needs no click at all; documented as optional.

Partners: praetorianer777/Stator and Cloudster1/Exciter use it for their "Connect Armature" button.

issues.title: Let a partner tool create its own webhook once an administrator agrees
issues.body:
Connecting a partner (Stator, Exciter) today means an Armature administrator adds a webhook by hand, picks the topics and copies a secret into the partner. A partner should be able to set up its own webhook once an Armature administrator agrees.

- `POST /api/v1/webhooks/partner` (or part of the OAuth consent for an administrator, scope `webhooks.manage`): the partner names its receiver URL and topics; Armature creates the endpoint, owned by the partner client, and returns the secret once.
- The administrator sees and can remove it in the webhook list, marked with the partner's name; the partner can rotate its secret and change its topics, never other endpoints.
- Armature's outbound guard still applies; if the receiver is refused, the answer says which value to add to `network.outboundAllow`.
- Capability `webhooks.partner@1` in `/api/v1/meta`.

issues.title: Offer webhook envelope version 2 in the CloudEvents shape
issues.body:
Armature, Stator and Exciter send webhooks in one shared envelope, version 1: `{version, id, topic, occurredAt, payload}` plus `source`. Version 2 follows the CloudEvents 1.0 specification, so any receiver, a future relay in Dynamo, or a standard broker understands it without tool-specific code.

- Structured mode (`application/cloudevents+json`): `specversion: "1.0"`, `id`, `source` (e.g. `/armature`, `/stator`, `/exciter`, or the instance's URL), `type` (e.g. `dev.armature.issue.updated`, `dev.stator.page.remote_link.removed`), `time`, `datacontenttype: "application/json"`, `data` (the version 1 payload), and the extension attribute `dataversion` for the payload's own version.
- Signatures stay as in version 1 (HMAC over the body, timestamped signature header), since CloudEvents leaves authentication to the transport.
- An endpoint chooses the version it receives when it is registered; version 1 stays the default and keeps working for at least one Dynamo release after version 2 ships. The receiver side accepts both.
- Event types are listed with their payloads in the tool's OpenAPI document (or a schema beside it) and in Dynamo's shared list (praetorianer777/Dynamo#4).
- Events stay thin: ids, keys and what changed, no content a subscriber's own rights might not cover.
- Capability `webhooks@2` in `/api/v1/meta` once supported, next to `webhooks@1`.

- Return straight away when `added` is empty.

issues.title: Match the start of words in issue descriptions with text ~
issues.body:
`text ~ "meta"` does not find an issue whose description says "metadata". In `backend/internal/nql/compile.go` the summary part matches any part of a word (`i.summary ILIKE '%' || $n || '%'`), but the description part needs whole words: `jsonb_to_tsvector('simple', i.description, '["string"]') @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $n)`. People searching as they type (Stator's issue search, praetorianer777/Stator#425) type the start of a word and expect it to match.

- Let `text ~` match the start of each word in the description too: build the tsquery from the typed words as prefixes, `word1:* & word2:*`. Build it from tokens Armature extracts itself, e.g. `to_tsvector('simple', $n)` lexemes joined with `:* &`, or strip everything but letters and digits from each word before appending `:*`, so the text never reaches `to_tsquery` as query syntax.
- `summary ~` stays a substring match; `description ~` (if it exists) gets the same prefix rule as `text ~`.
- Keep the index use in mind: a prefix tsquery still uses a GIN index on the description's tsvector, if there is one; if there is none, consider adding it.
- Tests: `text ~ meta` finds "metadata" in a description, `text ~ "data meta"` finds "metadata about data", and characters like `& | ! : * ( )` in the typed text are plain characters, never operators.

issues.title: A token exchange or a narrower consent drops a connected app's webhook scope
issues.body:
Since #296 and #297, a person has one grant per connected app, and a new grant replaces the old one's scopes (`grant()` upserts on `(user_id, client_id)`). Two paths give a narrower grant than the one a person already holds:

- The token exchange from a Keycloak token (`fromIdentityProvider`) never gives `webhooks.partner`, so it replaces an administrator's grant that held it.
- A later consent that asks for fewer scopes replaces the grant the same way.

What happens: an Armature administrator connects Stator with `webhooks.partner`, and Stator sets up its webhook. Later the same administrator signs in to Stator, and Stator trades their Keycloak token for a grant (Stator #430). Their grant now lacks `webhooks.partner` and its old refresh token has ended, so Stator can no longer change, rotate, test or recreate its own webhook until somebody connects it as an administrator again.

Asked: an exchange or consent keeps the scopes the existing grant already holds that the new request did not ask to drop, or at least keeps `webhooks.partner`. Alternatively, docs/oauth.md says that a new grant replaces the scopes, so partners ask for the union themselves.

Stator works around it meanwhile by exchanging only when it holds no grant for the person, and by asking an administrator for every scope at once.

issues.title: Add a suite demo filled with the issues of Armature, Exciter and Stator
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Armature together with Exciter and Stator, I want a demo whose issues are the suite's own development history, so that I see the three tools working on real, linked content rather than invented examples.

Part of one suite demo: Armature holds the issues, Stator the documentation (praetorianer777/Stator#457) and Exciter the requirements (Cloudster1/Exciter#270), and Exciter traces between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Adding it:** an administrator adds the suite demo once, from Settings > Installation beside "Add the demo project", and `make seed` adds it too. It is refused when one of its keys is taken.
- [ ] **Projects:** three projects, `ARM`, `EXC` and `STA`, hold the GitHub issues of `Cloudster1/Armature`, `Cloudster1/Exciter` and `praetorianer777/Stator`. Pull requests are left out.
- [ ] **Issues:** each keeps its GitHub number as its key (`EXC-261` is Exciter issue #261), its title, its Markdown body as a document, its labels and its milestone. Closed issues are done, with the date they closed.
- [ ] **Dependencies:** "Depends on" references become blocking links, also across projects (`Cloudster1/Exciter#59` in an Armature issue links to `EXC-59`).
- [ ] **People:** no GitHub login or email address is copied. Reporters and assignees are the seed's demo people.
- [ ] **Snapshot:** the content comes from a snapshot in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network. `make demo-snapshot` refreshes it with `gh` and records the date and commit of each repository.
- [ ] **Partners:** once Exciter and Stator add their part, the issues show their requirements and pages as remote links. Those tools push the links; Armature needs nothing new for that.

## Tests

- Go unit: the snapshot maps to issues (keys, states, closing dates, labels, milestones, people, "Depends on" links).
- Integration: add the demo; a second add and a taken key are refused; each project holds as many issues as its snapshot; a cross-project blocking link exists.
- Browser: add the demo from Settings, open `EXC-261` and see its blocking link, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- Beside `backend/internal/demo`, through `issue.ImportInput` with `KeyNum` for the GitHub number and `ExternalKey` set to the issue URL, so that a renewed snapshot updates the issues instead of copying them.
- One JSON file per repository; the keys join `demo.Keys` so the two demos never clash.
- A decision in `docs/decisions.md`: why a snapshot and not a live import from GitHub.

Depends on: nothing.

issues.title: Let people in by group mapping at sign-in and at token exchange
issues.body:
When an installation maps a Keycloak group to a role, a person in that group is already allowed in; they should not have to be invited or admitted from a join request first. Otherwise Stator and Exciter cannot connect a person to Armature at sign-in (the token exchange from #280 refuses anyone without standing), and people have to connect by themselves.

- At OIDC sign-in, a person without standing whose `groups` claim holds a group that has a role assignment is created and admitted with that role, then their groups are synced as today.
- The same at a token exchange from a partner app (`fromIdentityProvider` in `backend/internal/oauth/token.go`): a person who never opened Armature is connected by Stator or Exciter at their first sign-in there. The account is matched or created by verified email as at sign-in.
- A person in no mapped group still gets a join request, as today; a disabled person is refused.
- Off unless an administrator turns it on: `admitByGroup` on `PUT /api/v1/oidc-provider` (default false), so existing installations behave as before. The setting shows on the sign-in settings page with a sentence saying what it does.
- The audit log records each admission as admitted by group <name>.
- Tests: sign-in and exchange for a new person in a mapped group, in an unmapped group, and one disabled in Keycloak; with the setting off nothing changes.

**Here today:** `backend/internal/oidc/signin.go` refuses a person without standing (`ErrNotAMember`) and records a join request; `token.go` answers such a person `invalid_grant`.

issues.title: The chart's roles Job fails: Kubernetes turns $$ in its SQL into $
issues.body:
Installing the chart with the bundled Postgres fails: the roles Job never finishes, so the install's post-install hooks fail and every api and worker crash-loops on `password authentication failed for user "armature_app"`.

```
ERROR:  syntax error at or near "$"
LINE 1: DO $
```

`templates/job-roles.yaml` runs its SQL from the container's `args`, where Kubernetes reads `$$` as an escaped `$`, so `DO $$ ... $$;` reaches Postgres as `DO $ ... $;`. Stator's chart ran into the same and uses a named tag (`DO $roles$ ... $roles$;`) with a comment saying why.

- Use a named dollar-quote tag in the roles Job, and anywhere else the chart puts `$$` into a command or args.
- A test that installs the chart (as Stator's and Exciter's chart-install tests do) would have caught it; at least the golden render should not contain `$$` inside args.

Found by Dynamo's kind test, which installs Stator, Armature and Exciter together (praetorianer777/Dynamo#10).

issues.title: Show settings to administrators only and add a narrow layout
issues.body:
The three tools that run together (Stator, Armature, Exciter) are moving to one menu layout, described in praetorianer777/Dynamo#12. It follows Armature's sidebar, so Armature changes the least. This is Armature's part.

## Sidebar
- **Settings group:**
  - Show it to administrators only (`canAdministerOrg`). Today every agent sees all 13 entries, and most pages then refuse them.
  - Order: Installation, Access, Users, Single sign-on (if it gets a page of its own), Holidays, Workflows, Labels, Automation, Fields, Issue view, Webhooks, Audit log.
- **New "You" group** for the personal pages that are in Settings or reachable from nowhere today, in this order:
  - Your profile
  - Notification settings (the Notifications section of the profile)
  - Themes
  - Access tokens (today's "API tokens")
  - Connected apps (`/settings/connected-apps`, now only on the hub and by URL)
- **Saved searches** (`/filters`) joins the Work & Plan group, after Search.
- **Notifications:** rename the sidebar entry Inbox to Notifications, keep the route `/inbox`, and give it the unread badge the rail bell has.

## Rail
- The bell opens a panel with the latest notifications, "Mark all read", "See all" (`/inbox`) and "Notification settings", like the other two tools. Today it only navigates.
- With the sidebar folded, the avatar menu gains Settings (`/settings`, administrators) between Your profile and Sign out.

## Palette and hub
- **The palette** reaches every sidebar page, from the lists the sidebar reads.
  - Today its settings part is a fixed list that leaves out Installation, Automation, Webhooks, Fields, Issue view, Audit log, Connected apps and Profile.
  - Its settings entries follow the same administrator rule as the sidebar.
- **`/settings` hub:**
  - Add Issue view.
  - The Everyone card becomes Settings and is shown to administrators only.
  - The You card gets the "You" group's pages.

## Narrow screens
Armature is the one tool without a narrow layout.
- Below 768px, hide the rail and sidebar. A thin strip with an "Open the navigation" button opens a drawer with the same groups, and the theme switch and build stamp in its foot.
- Stator's and Exciter's `features/shell/Sidebar.tsx` and `state.ts` already do this, with `SIDEBAR_DRAWER_BELOW_PX = 768`.
- Read the width on resize, not only at mount.

## Done when
- A non-administrator sees no Settings group, and the palette offers them no settings page.
- Every page the hub lists is reachable from the sidebar or the "You" group, and from the palette.
- At 375px wide the drawer opens, holds every group and closes on following a link.
- The e2e suite checks the sidebar for an administrator and a member, and the drawer at phone width.

issues.title: Run the tests on every pull request, as Stator, Exciter and Rotor do
issues.body:
Stator, Exciter and Rotor each run their tests on GitHub for every pull request, every push to main and every night. Armature runs only the Conventions check there, so a pull request can be merged with a failing test layer and nobody sees it until someone runs `make test-all` by hand.

Add workflows of the same kind:

- **CI**: the four layers (`make test`, `make npm ARGS="run test"` with the typecheck, `make test-integration`, `make test-e2e`) and the chart's lint and golden render, as jobs side by side, on every pull request, on main and nightly. A run by hand can repeat the gate to show a flaky test.
- **Chart install**: install `deploy/charts/armature` with `values-demo.yaml` into a throwaway kind cluster, check the hook Jobs, the workloads and a sign-in, then upgrade it with no failed health check. Runs when something the chart installs changes, as in Stator and Exciter.
- **Deps**: govulncheck and npm audit, nightly and on a pull request that changes a dependency, as in Rotor. Not a required check.
