issues.title: The demo chart's seed Job fails when SeaweedFS is still starting
issues.body:
Installing the chart with `values-demo.yaml` sometimes fails at the post-install seed Job:

```
level=ERROR msg="seed failed" error="attachment bucket: check bucket armature-attachments: Head \"http://armature-seaweedfs-s3:8333/armature-attachments\": dial tcp 10.96.1.243:8333: connect: connection refused"
Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: failed post-install: 1 error occurred:
	* job armature-seed failed: BackoffLimitExceeded
```

The seed runs as soon as migrate has, and asks for the bucket once. On a fresh install SeaweedFS's master may still be electing a leader, so the S3 gateway refuses the connection. The Job's two tries come about ten seconds apart and both fail, and the install fails with them. The chart install test from #311 hit this on one of two runs.

The seed already gives Gitea a minute to start. It should give the object store the same wait.

issues.title: Two browser scenarios fail now and then on GitHub's runners
issues.body:
Since the CI workflow from #311 runs the browser suite on GitHub's runners, two scenarios fail now and then. They never failed in any local run.

- **an API token can be created and revoked**: failed in 3 of 5 runs (#312, twice on #316). It reads the page as soon as the path is `/settings/tokens` and expects "No tokens yet", but the list may still be loading, so the text holds only the sidebar:
  ```
  the list starts empty: "Collapse the sidebar\nHome\nSearch\n...\nSET" does not contain "No tokens yet"
  ```
- **a request is followed by somebody who was only named**: failed once (#312). It takes the first mail about the request that reaches the follower. On a slow runner, the request's receipt can go out after the follower was added, and reach them first:
  ```
  the mail says who did it: "We have your request HELZ81W0G-1: The lift is stuck ..." does not contain "added you"
  ```

The token scenario should wait for its empty list. The desk scenario should ask `mailFor` for the mail `saying: "added you"`, as other scenarios do when two mails about one issue may arrive in either order.

issues.title: Take Dynamo's realm with the token-exchange audience mappers
issues.body:
`realm-check` compares `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` with Dynamo's canonical realm on `main`. Dynamo is adding the audience mappers token exchange needs (praetorianer777/Dynamo#13, PR praetorianer777/Dynamo#15):
- `stator`: `armature`, `exciter`;
- `exciter`: `armature`, `stator`;
- `armature`: `exciter`.

Armature takes a partner's exchanged token only if its `aud` holds `armature`, so without the mapper on `stator` and `exciter`, Stator's and Exciter's sign-in exchanges at Armature are refused. Once Dynamo's PR is merged, this copy differs and `realm-check` fails, so both should land together. Stator pins this copy, so Stator follows from here.

## Done when
- `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` is Dynamo's realm byte for byte, and `realm-check` and the seed's realm test pass.

issues.title: Shard the browser suite in CI
issues.body:
In CI, the `e2e` job is the slowest: about 9 minutes in a single job on the last green `main`, so the whole run waits for it. Stator splits its browser suite into 4 jobs of 9 to 11 minutes, and Exciter into 2.

**Change:** shard the browser suite in CI with Playwright's `--shard=i/n`. Run a matrix of jobs, each with its own stack, and merge the blob reports into one HTML report (`merge-reports`). Keep the tests that need the installation to themselves, if there are any, in one shard or in a serial phase of their own, as Stator does with its instance phase.

## Done when
- CI's browser jobs each take at most about 4 to 5 minutes, and the merged report lists every test once.
- Running the suite locally without a shard is unchanged.

issues.title: Create the Go cache directories before a container mounts them
issues.body:
`make release VERSION=0.1.0` in a fresh clone failed inside its own test:

```
failed to initialize build cache at /gocache: mkdir /gocache/00: permission denied
```

**Cause:** the Go targets mount `.cache/gocache` and `.cache/gomod` into a container that runs as the caller (`-u $(UID):$(GID)`). In a fresh clone those directories don't exist yet, so Docker creates them for the mount, owned by root. The container can't write to them, and the caller can't remove them either.

**Fix:** make the cache directories an order-only prerequisite of every target that mounts them, created by `mkdir -p` as the caller, as Dynamo does with `$(GO_CACHE)`.

## Done when
- `make test` and `make release DRY_RUN=1 VERSION=x.y.z` work in a fresh clone, and `.cache` is owned by the caller afterwards.

issues.title: Bootstrap the first administrator and members from the chart, as Stator and Exciter do
issues.body:
Armature has no bootstrap. A new installation is owned by whoever signs up first (`auth.signup: first`). Stator and Exciter instead run a bootstrap Job: it creates the organization, its first local administrator from a Secret, and the members to let in before their first sign-in.

**Why it matters:**
- **Takeover window.** In a cluster, Armature's ingress is public once its pods are ready, and nothing has signed up yet. Whoever reaches it first owns the installation. In Dynamo's umbrella chart, `dynamo-connect` signs up first, but only after all three tools' hooks. That's minutes of an open installation on a public address.
- **Workaround in Dynamo.** Dynamo's chart carries `armatureAdmin` and makes the owner itself, while the other two take theirs from their own charts (praetorianer777/Dynamo#20).

**Change:** a bootstrap as in Stator's and Exciter's charts:
- `bootstrap.admin.email`, with the password from a Secret the chart makes when none is named (`<fullname>-bootstrap-admin`, keys `username` and `password`, random when blank, kept across upgrades);
- `bootstrap.members`: emails and roles let in before their first sign-in;
- a post-install/post-upgrade Job that applies them idempotently, before the app answers sign-ups;
- with a bootstrap, `signup` defaults to `closed`, so there's no first-come owner. `first` stays for a setup without the bootstrap.

## Done when
- `helm install` with `bootstrap.admin.email` set leaves an installation owned by that account, with no open first sign-up at any point, and the chart test checks it.
- Rerunning the Job on an upgrade changes nothing, and a password changed in its Secret is kept.

issues.title: Sign in silently when the identity provider already has a session
issues.body:
Someone signed in to Armature, Stator or Exciter through the suite's Keycloak realm, who then opens another of the three, lands on its sign-in page and has to click "Sign in". Keycloak still has their session, so the click sends them there and straight back, signed in, without a password. The click is all that's left, but it happens on every first visit and on every link from one tool to another. This was seen on a real Dynamo install, where Keycloak returns at once.

**Change:** on a visit without a session, Armature first tries a silent sign-in:
- **The request:** a top-level redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with `prompt=none`, the usual `state`, PKCE and `nonce`, and the page the person asked for.
- **Keycloak still has a session:** the callback signs the person in, as a normal sign-in does, with the same group mapping and membership checks, and returns them to that page.
- **No session** (`error=login_required`, `interaction_required` or `consent_required`): the callback shows the sign-in page as today, and remembers for the browser session (a short-lived cookie) that the silent try already failed, so there's no redirect loop and no second round trip on the next page.
- **Only when single sign-on is configured:** with local accounts only, nothing changes.
- **Not after signing out:** a sign-out sets the same marker, so the person isn't signed straight back in. With RP-initiated logout at the provider, the provider's session ends too.
- **Can be turned off:** a setting, for example `auth.silentSignIn` in the chart, on by default when an OIDC provider is set.

## Done when
- In the integration or browser tests, with a provider that has a session, opening a deep link without a session lands on that page signed in, with no click. Without a provider session, it lands on the sign-in page, and the next page doesn't redirect again.
- After signing out, the next visit shows the sign-in page.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `auth.silent-sign-in@1`, so the suite's tests can rely on it (praetorianer777/Dynamo#2).
